title: 2026-09-11 Research Notes — Exact Geometry of the Recovered Golden-Ratio Spiral
status: new project mathematical deductions from an already recovered equation
novelty_scope: These deductions are newly added to the project on 2026-09-11. The mathematics of logarithmic spirals is established and is not claimed as globally new.

new_deductions.finding: The project spiral contains an exact discrete scale ladder at quarter-turn intervals. This is stronger and more precise than saying it is merely 'golden-ratio-like'.
The recovered spiral meets every radial line at the same angle. The constant pitch supplies a real invariant for comparing diagrams, trajectories or fitted data to the recovered equation.
Curvature falls by the inverse golden ratio every quarter-turn. Thus the same quarter-turn that expands radius by phi reduces curvature by 1/phi.
Arc length between two spiral radii is directly proportional to their radial difference. This gives a simple length estimator once a and angular limits are defined.
Area grows with radius squared rather than with the same phi factor as radius. A quarter-turn multiplies local r^2 by phi^2.

equations: ln r = ln a + b theta
new_deductions.finding: Any claim that an observed path follows this spiral can be tested with a straight-line fit in (theta, ln r) coordinates. This makes the spiral falsifiable as geometry.
new_deductions.test_rule: Compare held-out error or information criteria rather than choosing the logarithmic spiral after seeing the pattern.

new_deductions.finding: Geometry and dynamics should be separated. Two drawn spirals are not yet counter-rotating vortices. Counter-rotation requires a time parameter and angular velocities with opposite signs or another explicit phase law.
new_deductions.promotion_rule: Use 'vortex' only when a velocity or phase field and circulation/vorticity are actually defined.

researcher_notes: This is one of the cleanest project research gains because every geometric result follows from a previously recovered equation rather than from added symbolism.
The constant-pitch and log-linear forms provide practical recognition tests for future images, diagrams and trajectories.
A future visualization should label radius scaling, curvature scaling and pitch angle separately.
